newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends lower Friday, but up on the week.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends lower Friday, but up on the week.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures reversed course to settle sharply lower Friday, ending an astounding eight-day speculative rally which hoisted prices to their highest levels since September 1995.
Traders said today's downturn was a technical correction to a well overbought market, bought on by the end of a nine-day dockworkers strike in Colombia.
"Because of the resolution of the Colombian strike, the market corrected," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast.

In the morning, a round of trade buying vaulted benchmark March to a new contract high of 142.60 cents a lb. But a lack of follow through and a heavy bout of heavy commission house selling quickly knocked prices into negative territory.

March delivery ended down 3.15 cents at 136.90 cents, just above the session low of 136.50 cents. Second-position May fell 3.75 cents to 131.30 cents, while the outer months closed 2.40 to 5.15 cents lower.
Despite today's losses, the March contract gained 12.90 cents -- or more than 10 percent -- this week amid persistent near-term supply concerns.

Heightening the supply woes this week was a work stoppage at Colombia's Pacific coast port of Buenaventura, which curtailed some 300,000 60-kg bags of coffee exports from the world's second-biggest grower. Dockworkers returned to work Friday morning, but trucker drivers demanding "standby" payments prevented operations from returning normal, port officials said.

Traders also cited as bullish talk this week top-producer Brazil's 1997/98 crop could be smaller than last season's, and news the Association of Coffee Producing Countries agreed to cut in coffee exports by 1.3 million bags between January and June 1997, including 300,000 bags of arabica beans.

On the charts, however, analysts and traders said the market is likely to pull back further. They said today's key reversal day, a higher high than Thursday's followed by a close below Thursday's low, was technically bearish.
Additionally, momentum indicators, such as the standard nine-day RSI (relative strength indicator) have seen overbought levels above 90 pct this week.
Volume Friday reached an estimated 10,188 lots.
